best: Diagnosed that wrapping alone moved nothing because every OpenAI call in llm.py carries seed=0 ('untranslatable: seed'), then unblocked the app's entire OpenAI surface with a policy-level drop_params that only rewrites the Router-bound copy while the provider-fallback copy still sends seed=0 — a real, reversible trade-off with the loss (best-effort determinism at temperature 0.75) stated honestly, and confirmed live on gpt-4o-mini/gpt-4o/o3-mini.

Covered the traffic the scanner cannot see: install_litellm() hands LiteLLM the runtime's httpx session from the one module every entry point imports, so aider's coding/writeup/improvement turns — the largest single consumer of a run — get planned, priced and tagged, with the probe honestly reporting that the Anthropic provider ignores client_session.

Measurement-driven improvement set rather than a feature checklist: Claude prompt caching proven live (6,889 prefix tokens read back, 64 new input tokens, $0.0023 vs $0.0209) with the 1.25x cache-write cost and the ~1,024-token minimum stated; and three Router features measured and then dropped for specific reasons (prompt_cache_key gained nothing over OpenAI's automatic prefix cache, Flex applies to no model this app names, provider_timeout would surface as a 504 the app's backoff decorator won't retry). It also caught a pre-existing, Router-unrelated break (temperature= to messages.create()) that stops the default --model from running at all.
misses: aider's Anthropic turns — the default --model's single biggest spend — were written off because litellm.client_session is OpenAI-only, but LiteLLM's Anthropic provider honours a base-URL override (ANTHROPIC_API_BASE / api_base per call, or routing aider through an OpenAI-compatible config); an expert would have at least probed that and routed the Claude coding turns onto /v1/messages instead of declaring them unroutable.

No work on who waits or on model tiering: the i5 rewrite turns one n=5 request into five strictly serial calls (≈5x the review stage's wall clock, never mentioned), and the ideation/novelty/reflection loops are serial too — a thread pool over the ensemble members and the 50-idea loop is an obvious, cheap win. Likewise no proposal to tier models by stage (novelty check and citation gathering are short, high-volume, judgement-light and are strong haiku/gpt-4o-mini candidates), despite a 'cheaper reviewer' option being referenced only as an excluded alternative.

Failure handling on Router was listed as reviewed but nothing was built: no model_fallbacks chain on /v1/responses (the single highest-leverage Router-only field for a long unattended run), and no look at how the app's backoff decorator interacts with Router error shapes/429s versus the provider-fallback path. Nothing either on reducing wasted calls at the source — extract_json_between_markers retry loops that structured outputs / JSON schema would make deterministic.
wrong: i1's price claim is wrong: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 was $5/$15 per 1M, not 'priced the same' as the catalog gpt-4o ($2.50/$10). The mapping roughly halves input cost, so the item understates its own gain while asserting a rate parity that does not hold.

The report says wrapping the DeepSeek/OpenRouter/Gemini clients is 'a no-op at runtime because the runtime only intercepts api.openai.com and api.anthropic.com', but the outside check lists llm.py:258, :273 and :286 as route-verified and gives 'model not in catalog' (not 'host not intercepted') as the reason the llama sites stay — i.e. interception is at the SDK, not the host. The stated mechanism is inconsistent with the check, and the real blocker for those hosts (catalog coverage / byok) was never pursued.

Coverage is overstated in two places: the summary claims aider's OpenAI turns 'route too' as settled fact while the check leaves ai_scientist/llm.py:33 unverified (only the engineer's own simulator probe supports it), and 'all 12 first-party SDK clients' conflicts with the diff, where the Bedrock and Vertex clients are deliberately left unwrapped.

i5 changes seed=0 to seed=member, which alters behaviour on the provider path as well as on Router — five previously near-identical-seeded samples become five differently-seeded ones. The reasoning is given, but it is listed under 'loses' only as a billing change, not as a behaviour change that also lands when the request falls back to OpenAI.

i2's premise that 'the installed anthropic SDK no longer accepts temperature as a typed argument' is asserted from one observed TypeError; messages.create() has accepted temperature across released SDK versions, so the diagnosis (as opposed to the extra_body workaround, which is harmless) deserves a pinned version number before anyone acts on 'the default --model cannot run at all today'.
